Because that's how networks work? When one thing is using up resources there is less for other stuff.

Steam is kind of like bit torrent in that it pulls from many locations to serve fast downloads.

Do a speed test, Do one while running steam, do one while running steam & streaming a 1080p youtube video, do one while running steam, streaming a 1080p video AND torrenting a linux .iso. Do one while doing all of that and cocaine. Notice how the speed drops on your network during all of them.

Resources get used by programs which means there's less for other programs like speed test.

A speedtest tests speeds by downloading. You need to add steams download speed to your speedtest, bearing in mind that steam measures speeds in megaBYTES per second, whereas speadtest.net uses megaBITS per second (a megaBIT is 1/8th of a megaBYTE). You are clearly saturating your connection between the speedtest and the steam download, so you need to add those numbers to get your actual speeds, hence why the upload speed is virtually unaffected. It should also be noted that Comcast, shitty as they are, do not throttle anymore (or at least in ways that are obvious, provable, and verifiable), I hate them for many reasons, but that is not one of them.

• Chinese does not have alphabet system; it has phonetic symbols to help learning pronunciation. Mainland China uses Han Yu Pin Yin, which is from Latin alpabet. Taiwan uses Zhu Yin . Taiwan, Hong kong, Macau, Malaysia and Singapore also use Wade–Giles System for romanization.
  • Chinese is single syllable language; each Chinese Character has only one syllable. But Chinese Mandarin has four tones which are extremely important in Spoken Chinese. Chinese seniors still can differentiate the tones. Different tones can convey totally different meanings.

  • One Chinese character may have multiple meanings and multiple pronunciations. The character's writing does not necessarily imply its pronunciation or meaning, although often related.

  • Chinese uses character（Hanzi/汉字/漢字） for reading and writing. They are not paintings;they are characters.Also, Chinese can write them with any kind of pen.There are two styles of written Chinese: traditional Chinese and simplified Chinese. Traditional Chinese is much harder to write and memorize, but much more vivid and descriptive. It is typically used in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau. Simplifed Chinese was designed to quickly decrease iliterate population (In early 1940s, 80% Chinese were iliterate). However, simplified Chinese is not as meaningful and beautiful as traditional Chinese. Now, it is typically used in Mainland China and Singapore.

  • Hanzi does not exclusively belong to Chinese(as an ethnic group). Japan also uses the similar system-Kanji. North Korea and South Korea also used the similar system-Hanjia, although they abandoned.
